alex (runtime): heads-up - just got an SEV from a customer (TICKET-4821) about p95/p99 spikes on chat-generation since last night

sam (support): details? which model/seq/route?

alex (runtime): model: redwood-chat-3b, typical seq 512, region us-west-2. baseline p95 ~120ms -> now ~420ms, p99 hitting 2.1s. started after the 02:15 deploy (rollout: rollout/2026-03-16-0215)

maria (oncall): alert graph: https://metrics.redwood.ai/alerts/4821 - looks correlated to kernel-selection change at 02:17

ingrid (ml infra): I queried the runtime logs for kernel selection, here's a snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T02:16:58Z kernel_selector: estimator_v2 selected flash_pref (flashattn_v2) for model redwood-chat-3b, seq=512, est_cost=0.12, measured_latency=0.78
2026-03-16T02:17:01Z kernel_selector: perf_check fallback sdpa_v1 selected after timeout
```

alex (runtime): suspicious: estimator_v2 should prefer SDPA for seq=512 on A100s due to memory layout. looks like cost model underestimates flashattn latency for this sequence distribution

sam (support): customer says it only affects their highest traffic routes, intermittent but high tail. they sent a sample request: content ~ 450 tokens

maria (oncall): mitigation options: 1) toggle kernel selector to disable flash_pref globally 2) patch estimator and canary 3) route affected customer to dedicated fallback pool. quickest is toggling the runtime flag for kernel preference

alex (runtime): agree. quick toggle command (admin endpoint):
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.ai/runtime-flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" -d '{"kernel_selector.prefer_flash": false}'
```
deploy-bot: rollout started for runtime flag change: rollout/flag-4190012345 -> targeting prod-us-west-2, prod-eu-1 (staged)

maria (oncall): executing toggle on prod-us-west-2 now

ci-bot: flag rollout finished on prod-us-west-2 (ok), prod-eu-1 (ok)

maria (oncall): monitoring... p95 dropping back toward baseline in prod-us-west-2: 420ms -> 140ms over 3 minutes

sam (support): gave customer temporary workaround: set "prefer_flash": false in their Dedicated pool routing; they're confirming

ingrid (ml infra): root cause hypothesis: estimator_v2 uses a simplified flop-based cost that misses kernel launch overhead at this token distribution. will create repro and run microbenchmarks today

alex (runtime): repro steps I'm using locally:
1) spawn loadgen with seq=450-520, batch=8 on A100 40GB
2) use model redwood-chat-3b quant=q4f16
3) run with kernel_selector=estimator_v2 and log kernel choice

command: 
```
./loadgen --model redwood-chat-3b --seq-min 450 --seq-max 520 --batch 8 --device a100 --kernel-estimator v2 --log-kernel
```

alex (runtime): observed flashattn chosen ~70% and p99 ~1.8s locally; forcing sdpa gives p99 ~0.22s

ingrid (ml infra): filing a PR to add a quick heuristic: if seq in [400,600] and batch<=8 then bias estimator toward sdpa. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/ml-infra/pulls/2749

maria (oncall): action items: alex/infr to validate PR with microbench, canary a small rollout, support to keep customer updated. I'll keep the flag off until we verify

sam (support): updated ticket TICKET-4821 with mitigation steps and ETA for fix, customer accepted temporary SLA credit

alex (runtime): follow-up: we'll add more detailed sampling to perf traces to capture kernel_estimator output in traces (so future incidents show estimator decisions)

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout of estimator patch: canary/estimator-v2-fix -> 03:30 UTC

ingrid (ml infra): I'll run the benchmark now and post raw numbers

ingrid (ml infra): benchmark results pasted: 
```
flashattn_v2: p95=380ms p99=1.9s
sdpa_v1: p95=120ms p99=230ms
bias-heuristic (patched): p95=130ms p99=240ms
```

alex (runtime): good. patch looks promising. schedule canary. once canary stable we'll re-enable prefer_flash in config but with estimator_v2 patched

maria (oncall): timeline: canary 03:30 -> monitor 30m -> if ok roll to full at 04:15

sam (support): I'll update customer around 03:50 with canary status

alex (runtime): postmortem notes to add: - estimator_v2 regression due to cost simplification - insufficient canary coverage for seq distribution edges - add autotests for seq 400-600 profiles - add quick runtime flag for kernel preference - improve ops runbook

maria (oncall): any blockers?

ingrid (ml infra): none. PR up, benchmarks green, canary scheduled

maria (oncall): thanks all. keeping channel open until rollback/complete :thumbsup:

sam (support): closing loop with customer after full roll/verify

alex (runtime): will post final postmortem and follow-ups in #postmortems once complete

(END)
